newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin meets Chernomyrdin in hospital ahead of op.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin meets Chernomyrdin in hospital ahead of op.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, waiting for doctors to decide when and whether to operate on his heart, met Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Tuesday in the hospital where he has spent the last 10 days.
Interfax news agency, quoting Kremlin sources, said the two men met for about an hour, discussing several issues including regional elections and the situation in breakaway Chechnya.
Six Russian soldiers were killed near the rebel region on Tuesday when their armoured personnel carrier went over a mine but a shaky truce agreed last month has generally held.

Yeltsin has already handed over some powers to Chernomyrdin before his planned heart operation and has said that the prime minister will take over during the surgery. Doctors are due to meet on Wednesday to decide when to operate.

But the operation, initially billed as simple heart bypass surgery, has been overshadowed by other doubts about the president's overall state of health after he moved to the elite Central Clinical Hospital.

Top Russian surgeon Renat Akchurin suggested at the weekend that the operation might be delayed for six to eight weeks -- or even cancelled. Akchurin, attending a medical conference in Moscow on Tuesday, is expected to lead the operation.
Akchurin also said Yeltsin had probably had a heart attack during the presidential election campaign.
Russian communists, defeated by Yeltsin in the July election, accused the president and his team of misleading the electorate by concealing information.

"(Concealing the heart attack) amounts to falsification. The elections were not fair," Communist Party leader Gennady Zyuganov told Reuters at the Council of Europe's parliamentary assembly in Strasbourg.

Yeltsin, who disappeared from the public eye during the two rounds of Russia's presidential election, admitted over a month later he needed an operation on his heart. His absence has created a power vacuum in Russia and top politicians have been jockeying for position in a possible race to succeed him.

But tight lips in the Kremlin -- press officers often answer questions with the stock phrase "We have no information on that" -- has focused attention on the international medical conference in Moscow's exclusive President Hotel.
The doctors' get-together has turned into a media circus where reporters and television crews almost outnumber doctors.
German heart surgeon Hans Borst said he thought the experts would happily advise Yeltsin.

"Logically the Russians should use the expertise presented by a group of at least 12 foreigners who are very well versed in this type of surgery," he said. "All of us are rather curious about what is going to be the next step."
Participants at the conference include pioneering U.S. surgeon DeBakey, who has already said he will join the team of doctors advising Yeltsin.

DeBakey, who works in Houston and is 23 years older than his new patient, conducted the world's first successful heart bypass operation. "I'm always optimistic," he said when he arrived in Moscow on Monday.
Yeltsin's prolonged stay in hospital has sent shudders through Russia's embryonic financial markets.
Russian shares fell an average of three percent on Monday and prices tumbled further on Tuesday.
"It's really crashing, moving down with even some panic among brokers," said Alexei Genkin, sales desk manager at Alfa-Capital.
